kimi_k2.5/001: The strategy uses iterative deepening alpha-beta search with a custom board representation optimized for fast move generation and undo operations. It prioritizes captures (which are mandatory), evaluates material advantage (kings valued higher than men), and includes positional bonuses for advancement and center control. The search explores progressively deeper ply until time runs out, ensuring a legal move is always returned.
kimi_k2.5/002: The strategy uses a minimax search with alpha-beta pruning to look ahead several moves. It evaluates board states based on material (men vs kings), advancement toward promotion, control of the center columns, and occupation of the back rank. The search depth adapts to the number of pieces remaining (deeper in endgames) and respects the mandatory capture rule by generating only capture moves when available. Moves are ordered to prioritize captures (especially multi-captures) to improve pruning efficiency.
kimi_k2.5/003:
The strategy employs a depth-limited minimax search with alpha‑beta pruning (depth 5) to look ahead several ply.  
All legal moves are generated on an 8×8 board representation. Captures are mandatory; if several capture sequences are possible the engine restricts itself to those that capture the maximum number of pieces (standard checkers rule). Multi‑jump captures are fully explored with a depth‑first search that handles king promotion during the turn.  
The evaluation function scores material (men = 100, kings = 180), rewards advancement toward the king row, gives a small bonus for kings near the center, and protects the back rank. This combination produces strong tactical play while staying well within the 1 second time limit.

Non-capture moves are searched to minimize immediate loss and maximize positional advantage.

kimi_k2.5/006: The strategy for this policy is to use an alpha-beta search with a custom evaluation function. The agent first checks for mandatory captures using a recursive search that handles multi-jump sequences (including promotion during a capture sequence). The evaluation function considers material (kings valued higher than men) and positional advancement (rewarding progress toward promotion).
